## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-27 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Settings → People → Staff; /admin/staff · owner, practice admin.
Findings and reviewers: F-30 · reviewers A-23, C-14, C-15.
Rationale: A practice admin is offered Offboard on the owner doctor and the dialog opens; the code refuses only the last administrator. If it goes through, a hired admin ends the owner's access and moves the owner's patients to Needs rebooking. A role cannot be changed without offboarding and inviting again. /admin/staff is a second invite flow reachable only by typing the address.
Proposed UX behaviour: First, a test on real PostgreSQL records what the server does today when a practice admin offboards an owner. Then: only an owner may offboard an owner, and never the last owner; the server refuses anyone else. Any offboarding asks for the identity step-up. The Offboard button is absent on rows the signed-in user may not offboard and on their own row, with a short reason in words. Change role is offered on a staff row: it takes effect on the next request, ends sessions that hold the old role, and is audited. /admin/staff is either linked from Settings → People or removed with its route.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: Staff table row actions; the existing Dialog and step-up. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Back end: the owner rule, step-up on the offboard endpoint, the change-role endpoint with policy and audit. Front end: row actions, dialog.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code.
Clinical sign-off: Decision required before merge: question 18 of the validation plan (may a practice admin remove a doctor, or only the owner), recorded on the issue.
Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: authorisation and sessions. ponytail-review and a mutation check are required by the house rules for anything touching auth.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Custom roles (exist). (2) Bulk changes. (3) Compact rows on the staff table (after-pilot table ticket).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a practice admin and an owner, when the admin calls the offboard endpoint for the owner on main, then a test records the answer and the issue states it
- [ ] **AC2.** Given a practice admin, when the offboard endpoint is called for an owner, then the server answers 403 and nothing changes
- [ ] **AC3.** Given one owner, when anyone tries to offboard them, then the server refuses
- [ ] **AC4.** Given any offboarding, when it is confirmed without a recent step-up, then the server asks for it
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a receptionist, when an owner changes her to nurse, then her next request has the nurse's access, her old sessions end, and the audit log holds who, when, from and to
- [ ] **AC6.** Given the integration tests, when the owner rule or the step-up requirement is removed, then a test fails
- [ ] **AC7.** Given the staff table, when a user may not offboard a row, then no Offboard button is offered there; axe finds no violation in English or Arabic
- [ ] **AC8.** Given the app, when /admin/staff is opened, then it is linked from Settings or answers Page not found

## Test notes

- Integration (real PostgreSQL): owner rule, last owner, step-up, change role, tenant isolation.
- Playwright (tests/e2e/staff.spec.ts, access-ended.spec.ts; J1 offboard step): change a receptionist to a nurse; an admin sees no Offboard on the owner.

## Notes / open questions

- Regression risk: medium.
- Kept in the pilot phase although it is in wave S3: it is an authorisation question, and the house security check ranks it before polish.
